cleanIntro: This guide follows Beretta's manual for its side-by-side family, which never prints the 486 Parallelo name, so check your variant against it. A side-by-side comes apart into three pieces and back together in a minute, so the job is less about disassembly than about two surfaces: the bores, and the hinge pin area where the receiver and fore-end iron carry the load of every shot. Beretta is emphatic about the second one.

steps.title: Muzzles safe, safety on
steps.action: This guide follows Beretta's side-by-side family manual, which does not name the 486 Parallelo, so check your variant against it. Point the barrels in a safe direction and move the safety back until the letter S is fully visible.
steps.prose: Everything after this is done with the gun pointed somewhere a discharge would hurt nobody. The safety goes on first because the next move opens the gun with your hand near the trigger.
steps.quote: engage the safety by moving it back; the letter “S” must be fully visible
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — USE — LOADING AND FIRING, printed p.15

steps.title: Top lever right, barrels down, chambers emptied by hand
steps.action: Turn the top lever to the right and tilt the barrels down. Spent shells are thrown clear; unfired cartridges are only raised, so lift them out with your fingers and look into both chambers until you can see they are empty.
steps.prose: The extractors lift a live round just far enough to grip it. A cartridge left half-raised in one chamber is the classic miss on a two-barrel gun, so look at both.
steps.quote: When the shotgun is opened after shooting, the extractors will eject the spent shells and raise the unfired cartridges to make manual removal easier.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — USE — UNLOADING, printed p.17

steps.title: Unloaded before anything comes apart
steps.action: Before the fore-end comes off, confirm once more that both chambers are empty. Beretta puts this demand at the head of the disassembly chapter, in capitals.
steps.prose: On a break-open this is the easiest check in shooting, and that is exactly why it gets skipped. It takes two seconds with the gun already open.
steps.quote: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THAT THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED BEFORE BEGINNING DISASSEMBLY PROCEDURES.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Fore-end catch lever down
steps.action: Close the gun, then pull the fore-end catch lever down. It releases the fore-end from the barrels; nothing under it is spring-loaded against you.
steps.prose: The fore-end is what holds the barrels to the hinge pins once the gun is open, so it comes off first with the gun closed.
steps.quote: Pull the fore-end catch lever down
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Fore-end forward and off
steps.action: Turn the fore-end forward and take it off the receiver. It comes away as one piece with its iron.
steps.prose: Set it down iron-side up. The fore-end iron's mechanism is one of the areas Beretta singles out for cleaning and oil, and it picks up grit from a bench.
steps.quote: Turn the fore-end forward to remove it from the receiver
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: ⛔ Top lever right, and HOLD the barrels as they tip
steps.action: Turn the top lever to the right and tilt the barrels down, holding them firmly. Without the fore-end there is nothing to stop them sliding off the hinge pins and onto the floor.
steps.prose: This is the step where barrels get dropped. Keep one hand under them the whole time the lever is open.
steps.quote: Tilt the barrels downward, holding them firmly to stop them from sliding off the hinge pins completely and falling
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Barrels up and out
steps.action: Lift the barrels gently up and out of the receiver. You now have the three pieces: barrels, fore-end, and stock with receiver.
steps.prose: No force is needed at any point. If the barrels resist, the lever is not fully over or the fore-end is not fully off.
steps.quote: Gently lift the barrels up and out of the receiver
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.18

steps.title: Snap caps out, and never dry-fire without them
steps.action: If you put snap caps in to let the hammers down, take them out of the barrels now. Tilting the barrels down recocks the hammers, so if you want the springs at rest for storage, decock again on snap caps, never on empty chambers.
steps.prose: Dropping a hammer on an empty chamber hits the firing pin with nothing to stop it. Beretta's answer is its snap caps, which let the gun be dry fired without damage.
steps.quote: It is equally important not to decock the hammers by pulling the trigger on an unloaded shotgun without snap-caps; the action could damage the firing pins.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — USE — DECOCKING THE HAMMERS, printed p.17

steps.title: Clean at the end of every day, chokes checked
steps.action: At the end of each day's hunting or shooting, clean the gun and check the chokes are properly tight. Where the metal has no protective surface treatment, clean and lubricate it thoroughly after every use.
steps.prose: Beretta ties the choke check to the clean on purpose. A choke that works loose while you shoot is a bore obstruction in the making.
steps.quote: At the end of a day of hunting or shooting, clean the shotgun and make sure the chokes are properly tightened.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20

steps.title: ⛔ Rod in from the CHAMBER end, every time
steps.action: Put a cotton cloth soaked in good gun cleaner on the rod, with a bronze brush if the residue needs it, and always enter at the cartridge chamber. Then run a clean dry cloth through to take the cleaner out, and finish with a lightly oiled cotton cloth.
steps.prose: Entering from the muzzle drags grit across the crown and the choke threads. And lightly means lightly: Beretta warns that built-up oil attracts dirt, and that excess oil or grease can obstruct the bore.
steps.quote: Always insert the cleaning rod into the cartridge chamber
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20

steps.title: Inner face of the receiver, but keep oil OUT of the pin holes
steps.action: Clean the inner face of the receiver, especially around the firing pin holes, and oil it lightly. No oil goes into the firing pin holes themselves.
steps.prose: Oil in the pin holes thickens, slows the pins and gives light strikes in the cold. Lightly is the operative word here.
steps.quote: Do not allow oil to enter the firing pin holes
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.20

steps.title: ⛔ The hinge pin area must never be dry
steps.action: Clean and lightly oil the fore-end iron mechanism and the barrel hook, and make sure the hinge pin area is lubricated, every time. This is the coupling that takes the load of every shot.
steps.prose: Beretta is plain that if these surfaces are not properly oiled, parts can seize or the gun can malfunction. It is the one area of the gun that is never left dry.
steps.quote: The hinge pin area is a very important coupling area. The surfaces of the receiver and foreend iron are subject to very high loads and if not properly oiled, could cause parts to seize or the shotgun to malfunction.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.21

steps.title: Outside wiped down; gun and case dry before storage
steps.action: Wipe every outer surface free of dirt, sweat and fingerprints and put a thin layer of good gun oil over it with a soft cloth. Then check that the gun and its case or bag are both perfectly dry before it goes away.
steps.prose: A damp case will rust a gun that was put away clean, which is why Beretta names the case and not only the gun.
steps.quote: Before putting away the shotgun, always check its condition and that of the case or bag. Make sure everything is perfectly dry: moisture or water droplets can damage the shotgun.
steps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.21

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard screws out — note front and back
deepSteps.action: With the barrels and fore-end off, take the trigger guard screws out with a screwdriver and note which went in front and which went at the back. Then unscrew the trigger guard counter-clockwise.
deepSteps.prose: The two screws go back in their own holes. Lay them out in order on the bench so the note is the layout itself.
deepSteps.quote: Use a screwdriver to remove the screws (A) from the trigger guard. Note the proper positions for reassembly (front and back).
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK DISASSEMBLY, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: Butt plate off, stock bolt out with its three washers
deepSteps.action: Take the butt plate screws out with a crosshead screwdriver and remove the butt plate. Put the supplied Allen key into the hex head of the stock bolt, unscrew it and take it out complete with its compression washer, limpet washer and convex washer, then take the stock off the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: The three washers are different and go back in one order only. Note it before they leave the bolt.
deepSteps.quote: Unscrew and remove the bolt, complete with compression washer (F), limpet washer (G) and convex washer (H): be sure to note the order for refitting.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK DISASSEMBLY, printed p.19

deepSteps.title: ⛔ And that is the end of what Beretta publishes
deepSteps.action: Past the stock there is nothing in this book for an owner. No repairs without the experience or training for them, no alterations or adjustments to any part, original Beretta spare parts only. Anything the gun needs to function goes to the manufacturer or a qualified person.
deepSteps.prose: This guide stops where Beretta stops.
deepSteps.quote: Any alteration or intervention necessary for the shotgun to function must be carried out by the manufacturer or by a qualified person.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Side by Side Shotgun User Manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — MAINTENANCE, printed p.21

cleaning.name: BORES
tasks: Clean at the end of every day's shooting and check the chokes are properly tight
Rod always in from the CHAMBER end, never the muzzle
Gun cleaner on a cotton cloth, bronze brush only if needed
Dry cloth through to remove cleaner residue, then a light oil
⛔ Never too much oil: excess oil or grease can obstruct the bore

cleaning.name: RECEIVER FACE
tasks: Inner face cleaned, especially round the firing pin holes
⛔ Oil lightly, and never INTO the firing pin holes

cleaning.name: HINGE PIN & FORE-END IRON
tasks: Fore-end iron mechanism and barrel hook cleaned and lightly oiled
Hinge pin area lubricated every time

cleaning.name: OUTSIDE & STORAGE
tasks: Dirt, sweat and fingerprints off every outer surface
Thin layer of good gun oil on a soft cloth
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges
⛔ Gun AND case perfectly dry before it is put away

reassembly: If the stock was off: refit it in reverse order, the three washers on the stock bolt in their noted order and the trigger guard screws in their noted front and back positions.
⛔ Never put the barrels into the receiver with the fore-end fitted on them.
Press the pin to raise the extractors, then put the barrels' front lug into its recess in the receiver.
Turn the top lever to the right and hold it there, complete the lug insertion, then release the lever.
Swing the barrels gently upward to close the gun.
Fore-end onto the receiver radius, turned toward the barrels and pressed onto them to engage the fore-end catch.
Beretta's check that the fore-end is locked: the top lever has returned to its original position.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: the gun closes without force and the top lever has clicked back into position; the fore-end is firmly locked to the barrels. Move the safety back until the letter S is fully visible, then open and close the gun once more to confirm the barrels seat cleanly.
